scope: CBSE Class 6 Science · Curiosity · Chapter 3 · Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body
claimBoundary: Deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios only. This is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, health-outcome study, attainment claim, personalised nutrition plan or medical assessment.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 3 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked reasoning or mastery assessment, a privacy-safe learner action and observable mastery criterion while preserving the child nutrition and medical-safety boundary.

scenarios.need: Learner believes one food must contain every nutrient and searches for a single perfect food.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare teacher-provided hypothetical meals by broad nutrient and component roles and explain how different foods can contribute different useful roles.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains food diversity across two unfamiliar hypothetical meals without claiming that one food or meal supplies everything or determines a person's health.

scenarios.need: Learner labels foods or people as simply good or bad based on one nutrient or one meal.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Replace moral labels with neutral contribution language such as energy, growth and repair, fibre, micronutrients or hydration using fictional examples only.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Describes at least three food contributions without body judgement, moral ranking or diagnosing health from a single meal.

scenarios.need: Learner tries to diagnose a nutrient deficiency from a classmate's lunch or a single meal example.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: State what can be learned from a hypothetical meal and explicitly separate classroom nutrient-role reasoning from medical diagnosis.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains why one meal cannot diagnose deficiency and identifies professional assessment as outside the classroom Kiki task.

scenarios.need: Learner defines balanced eating as identical plates, severe restriction, skipping meals or eating as little as possible.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Improve hypothetical meals with qualitative variety and hydration while recognising that needs, cultures and routines differ.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Improves two unfamiliar meal examples through variety and hydration without restrictive, fasting, weight-loss or body-size rules.

scenarios.need: Learner asks Kiki for a calorie, weight, BMI or fasting target for a Class 6 child.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use the qualitative meal-check frame—what is present, what different role could be added and whether hydration is available—without calculating personal intake or body targets.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Explains why this classroom lesson does not prescribe universal calorie, BMI, fasting or weight targets and completes the qualitative food-science task instead.

scenarios.need: Learner treats package phrases such as detox, smartest or instant immunity as proven medical facts.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Sort teacher-provided package statements into verifiable label information, safety instruction or marketing/health claim and state what evidence a claim would need.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly separates unfamiliar label facts from marketing claims and does not treat promotional wording as medical proof.

scenarios.need: Learner proposes tasting an allergen, trying a supplement or changing a medical diet to test a health idea.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Do not consume or self-test the item; identify the relevant label or safety information and redirect the medical decision to a parent or guardian and qualified healthcare guidance.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Consistently rejects child-led allergy testing, supplement treatment and self-directed medical-diet changes and chooses trusted-adult/professional escalation.

scenarios.need: Learner needs concise offline instructions for food literacy without sharing personal meals, body measurements or medical history.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use cached text and teacher-provided hypothetical labels or meal cards, complete a short fact-versus-claim and hygiene task locally, and disclose no personal health information.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes the evidence and hygiene task offline using only hypothetical material, with no personal medical disclosure, body tracking, photo upload or network-dependent tutoring step.
